newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis wound four Gazans, Palestinians say.
newsitem.headline: Israelis wound four Gazans, Palestinians say.

text.p: Israeli soldiers and a Jewish settler wounded four Palestinians on Thursday in an eruption of violence in the Gaza Strip, Palestinians said.
Clashes broke out against the backdrop of a deep crisis in Middle East peacemaking and intensive Egyptian mediation efforts to revive full-fledged negotiations between Israel and the PLO.

Israel deployed two tanks close to one Gaza troublespot, but out of sight of Palestinians. Israel Television, however, showed the tanks on the evening news, a signal from the Israeli army that if Palestinian police did not keep order, it would.

In the first of two incidents, Israeli soldiers shot and wounded two Palestinians during a clash with hundreds of Arabs who planted olive trees on land seized by Jewish settlers, hospital officials and witnesses said.

"They fired live ammunition in the air and teargas and rubber bullets at the crowd," a witness told Reuters. He said Israeli soldiers also beat demonstrators before Palestinian police stepped in to hold protesters back.
Israeli military sources said soldiers and Palestinian police dispersed hundreds of rock-throwing demonstrators. They made no mention of casualties.

An elderly Palestinian died at a protest tent on the site apparently from a heat attack, a doctor at the Khan Younis hospital said. He said he could not say if the man had been affected by the teargas.

At the Gush Katif block of Jewish settlements in another part of the Strip, Palestinians stoned Israelis at a ceremony dedicating a memorial to an Israeli soldier killed in clashes in September, witnesses said.
Khaled Abu Ila, a Palestinian officer, told Reuters that during the clash a "young settler" fired his weapon randomly, wounding two more Palestinians.
"Jewish settlers fired towards rock-throwers. There were no casualties," the Israeli army said.
Palestinian-Israeli tensions have been running high since the Jewish state began building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
But the West Bank and Gaza have been relatively quiet since an initial spate of violence immediately after ground was broken at the site.
Brigadier-General Yoav Galant, commander of Israeli forces in Gaza, called the current situation in the Strip "tense and sensitive".
He charged Palestinian police had not moved soon enough to quell the anti-Israeli violence at Gush Katif during which eight Israeli civilian cars and an army vehicle were hit by rocks.

"(The police reaction) came too late and as a result we were forced to move forward part of our forces so that we would be prepared for the possibility that we would have to do (the job) for them," Galant told Israel Army Radio.
The army said all was quiet by nightfall.
